swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,050-yard steady-state session built around longer freestyle repeats at a controlled, consistent tempo to develop your aerobic engine.

lift.title: Today's Lift

newsItems.title: Korstanje's comeback hits another wall
newsItems.body: Nyls Korstanje returned to competition at the Aachen Swim Festival, a moment worth celebrating on its own. But the Dutch Olympian suffered an injury setback during the meet, making what looked like a promising return a lot more complicated.

newsItems.title: Three Masters world records in one meet
newsItems.body: Ashley Twichell, Kelly Palace, and Penny Noyes each broke Masters world records at a short course meters meet hosted by TAC. Three swimmers, three world records, one session — that's a good day at the pool by any standard.

newsItems.title: 18-year-old Hein breaks South American record — again
newsItems.body: Agostina Hein returned from surgery and promptly swam her way to a 4th South American Record and 12th national record, this time in the short course IM events. The 18-year-old Argentine is making a strong case for being one of the most exciting young swimmers in the hemisphere.

newsItems.title: SDSU runs the streak to 88
newsItems.body: San Diego State defeated Pepperdine 84-59 at Raleigh Runnels Memorial Pool, extending their dual-meet winning streak to 88 consecutive victories. At some point a streak stops being a streak and starts being an institution.

athlete.name: Florent Manaudou
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Oleg Bkhambri (Voltmetro), CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Florent Manaudou is a French competitive swimmer born on 12 November 1990, with a French father and a Dutch mother. He joined the swimming club of Marseilles and later the French Army in 2009. He is the younger brother of Laure Manaudou, a 2004 Olympic gold medalist, and the two are the first siblings to both win Olympic gold medals in swimming. For his 2012 performances, he was awarded the Knight of the French National Order of the Légion d'Honneur.

Manaudou is an Olympic champion, world champion, and multiple-time world record holder, regarded as one of the greatest sprinters in history. He won Olympic gold in the 50-meter freestyle at the 2012 London Olympics and three gold medals at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships. He broke world records in the 50-meter backstroke and freestyle at the 2014 World Short Course Championships and won six medals at those same championships, including three golds.
